input.content: Pattern: "simplification" refactors that delete a conditional guard before a mutating call. In cleanup.py cleanup_setup(store, workspace_id, setup_id), the guard `if association and association["setup_id"] == setup_id` before `store.active.pop(workspace_id, None)` was removed. This is NOT dead code — it enforces that a workspace's active association is only cleared when it belongs to the setup being cleaned up. Removal makes a cleanup of a stale/superseded setup unconditionally clobber the workspace's *currently active* setup. Signal of the asymmetry: `store.pending` is keyed per-setup_id while `store.active` is keyed per-workspace_id, implying multiple setups per workspace can coexist, so cleanup is callable for a non-active setup. Lesson: a guard comparing an identity field before a pop/delete is a correctness invariant; verify no stale-call path exists before deleting it.
